punchline: Enron's board approved Fastow's LJM1 in one hour, between a stock split and a new corporate jet.
thirty_sec: On 28 June 1999 Enron's board met by phone for one hour. Among the items, besides a stock split and a new corporate jet, was LJM1, an entity run by chief financial officer Andrew Fastow that would hedge Enron's Rhythms stock. A Senate subcommittee later found the board had little time to study it, and that when the hedge was unwound Enron paid LJM1 a $30 million termination fee. The Finance Committee had never reviewed the proposal.
